questions.q: Where is Navigation Style (Standard vs. Console) chosen when building a Lightning app?
options: On the App Options step of the New Lightning App wizard
On a separate page reached only after the app is fully built
It can only be set via Apex, not in Setup
On the Navigation Items step
questions.explain: The App Options step of the app-creation wizard is where Navigation Style — Standard or Console navigation — is chosen.

questions.q: What does Console navigation let a user do that Standard navigation does not?
options: Access the utility bar, which Standard navigation cannot have
Open records as subtabs inside one workspace, jumping between related records without losing their place
Personalize their navigation bar past 50 items
Use Multiple Currencies
questions.explain: Console navigation opens records as subtabs in a single workspace tab, which is exactly the subtab/multi-record behavior Standard navigation doesn't offer.

questions.q: What does the utility bar provide, and which navigation styles can have one?
options: A fixed footer with docked tools, available with either Standard or Console navigation
A fixed footer with docked tools, available only with Console navigation
A sidebar of recent records, available only with Standard navigation
A popup window that opens a new browser tab
questions.explain: The lesson states that whichever navigation style is chosen, an app can also have a utility bar — it isn't exclusive to Console navigation.

questions.q: On the Utility Items step, what do Panel Width and Panel Height control?
options: The overall browser window size
How big the docked panel is when a user opens that specific utility
The number of utility items allowed on the bar
The font size used inside the utility bar
questions.explain: Panel Width and Panel Height are per-utility settings controlling the size of the docked panel that opens for that utility, not the whole screen.

questions.q: Why does the lesson describe console-style apps as the default shape for Service Cloud-style work?
options: Because console apps are required by Salesforce for any object with cases
Because support agents constantly jump between related records and need quick tools without losing their current screen — exactly what console navigation plus a utility bar provides
Because Standard navigation is being deprecated
Because console apps don't require a Navigation Items configuration
questions.explain: The lesson explains that the combination of console navigation (subtabs) and a utility bar (docked tools) matches the high-volume, multi-record nature of support work.
